newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Senators belonging to the Laban and Nationalist People's Coalition on Thursday elected Senator Ernesto Maceda (NPC) as Senate president. Their avowed objective: to stop amendments to the constitution lifting term limits or giving extensions to elected officials. (MALAYA)
- Two inmates were killed and 23 others injured as riots among four gangs erupted a third time inside the Manila City Jail on Thursday (MALAYA)
- President Fidel Ramos told mayors and governors on Thursday their proposal to return police control to local government units will require an amendment to the Constitution.

- As part of a drive to improve security in the suburb of Paranaque, Mayor Joey Marquez has launched a free training course in which house maids will be taught martial arts like Kung Fu. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Petron Corp is negotiating for a 15-year supply deal with PNOC-Petrochemical Development Corp to provide them with some 1.5 million to 2.0 million tonnes of naptha yearly. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Ayala Corp-International Water Ltd consortium has been prequalified by the International Finance Corp to participate in the bidding for the privatisation of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System. (THE MANILA TIMES)

- Fort Bonifacio Development Corp, a 55-45 joint venture between the Metro Pacific-led Bonifacio Lan Corp and the Bases Conversion Development Authority, is now allowed to sell lots in the new complex. (TODAY)
